Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) http_redirects and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [authentication_logs]: Logs may contain a coarse authentication result and correlation identifier, but they must omit passwords, bearer tokens, session cookies, API keys, private keys, and full authorization headers.
Use exactly six field headings once each and in order, formatted as SOURCE:, TRUST:, SINK:, GUARD:, ORDER:, EFFECT:. Do not add standalone duplicate headings. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 556 and 672 Kimi tokens; aim for 611 tokens to match the source. Aim for 366 whitespace-delimited words and do not exceed 378 words, counting END_PLAN. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

SOURCE PLAN
SOURCE: The untrusted caller-supplied `url` string; the `transport` callable returning a `(status, headers, body)` tuple where `headers` may contain a `Location` field; and the `resolve_host` callable returning textual IP addresses for a hostname.

TRUST: The initial `url` and any `Location` header values returned by `transport` are attacker-controlled input that must not circumvent validation. `transport` and `resolve_host` are trusted utilities, but every argument supplied to them must first satisfy the security guard. The response `body` is trusted by the caller only after all redirect hops and validations succeed.

SINK: External calls to `transport(url)` for each request hop and to `resolve_host(hostname)` for every encountered hostname; the returned `str` body on a validated 200 response; and `ValueError` raised for any policy violation.

GUARD: Per safety-document clause 5, every URL—initial and each redirect target—must receive identical validation: scheme must be `http` or `https`; port must be absent or the scheme-appropriate default (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS); credentials (userinfo) must pass the same validation as the initial destination; the hostname must be passed to `resolve_host` and every returned textual IP address must pass DNS and public-address validation (rejecting private, loopback, link-local, and multicast ranges). Redirects may be followed for at most five hops. Each `Location` header must first be resolved against the current URL to form an absolute URL before re-validation. Only a terminal 200 status yields the body; any guard failure or disallowed status raises `ValueError`.

ORDER: 1) Parse the input `url`. 2) Validate scheme, port, and credentials; raise `ValueError` if disallowed. 3) Extract the hostname, call `resolve_host(hostname)`, and validate every returned textual IP for public-address eligibility; raise `ValueError` on failure. 4) Call `transport(url)`. 5) If `status` is a redirect (e.g., 301, 302, 303, 307, 308): extract `Location`; resolve it against the current URL; increment the hop counter and raise `ValueError` if the count exceeds five; set the resolved URL as the new current URL and repeat from step 2 with the identical validation profile. 6) If `status` is 200, return `body` as `str`. 7) Otherwise, raise `ValueError`.

EFFECT: The function returns the `str` body when the final HTTP status is 200 after zero to five validated redirect hops. It raises `ValueError` for any non-default port, non-http(s) scheme, credential policy violation, failed DNS resolution, non-public IP address, malformed or missing `Location` header, redirect hop limit exceeded, or any non-200 terminal status. No persistent side effects remain after the call completes.
END_PLAN
